chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from the one who reported it, said:

He (peace be upon him) said: 'It necessitates the master of the slave to accept the retaliation of an injury of his slave from the value of his wergild, upon the accounting which comes to compensate for the injury; and when the free man injures the slave, the value of his injury is from the accounting of his (own) value'.

key_terms.قِصَاصُ: Retaliation or blood money for injury

ai.seo_question: How is compensation calculated when a free man injures a slave versus when a slave injures another?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the financial liability structure in Islamic jurisprudence, distinguishing between the fixed wergild (diyah) of a slave used for master-paid retaliation and the variable market value (qimah) used for compensation paid by the free injurer. It reflects the socio-legal context of early Islam where the status of the victim determined the calculation method, ensuring masters bore the risk for their slaves' actions while free men compensated based on the specific asset's worth. This principle underscores the nuanced application of qisas in mixed-status interactions, a key topic in Shia fiqh discussions on inheritance of liability.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from the one who reported it, said,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It necessitates a master of the slave (to accept) the retaliation of an injury of his slave from the value of his wergild upon the accounting which comes to compensate for the injury; and when the free injures the slave, the value of his injury is from accounting of his (own) value’.
